chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from 'Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

When you intend to perform the ghusl (ritual bath) of the deceased, place between yourself and him a cloth that covers his private parts, whether it is a shirt or something else. Then begin with his two hands, and wash his head three times with lotus leaves, then the rest of his body, and begin with his right side. When you want to wash his private part, take a clean rag and wrap it around your left hand, then insert your hand from beneath the cloth that is over the private part of the deceased and wash it without seeing his private parts. When you have finished washing him with lotus leaves, then wash him another time with water, camphor, and some of his hanut, then wash him with pure water in another washing. When you have completed three washings, place him in a clean cloth, then dry him.

key_terms.بِالسِّدْرِ: with lotus leaves, used in the first washing
key_terms.بِمَاءٍ وَكَافُورٍ: with water and camphor, used in the second washing
key_terms.حَنُوطِهِ: his funerary perfume or scenting substance
key_terms.عَوْرَتَهُ: his private parts that must be covered
key_terms.غُسْلَ الْمَيِّتِ: the ritual washing of the deceased

ai.seo_question: How should the ghusl (ritual bath) of a deceased person be performed according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the procedure for the ghusl (ritual bath) of the deceased, including covering the 'awrah, the order of washing, and the three washings with sidr, camphor, and pure water. It reflects the juridical etiquette and rulings related to taharah (ritual purity) and the dignified preparation of the deceased before shrouding.
